# Week 1 Mini-Studio

**[Back to Week 1 overview](index.qmd)**

This page follows the same sequence as [week1-code.R](week1-code.R). It is designed as a stable seminar companion: read the code, run the matching block in R or RStudio, then answer the short prompts here in words. That keeps the focus on the class code, which is the style you are most likely to meet in the exam.

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to use this page

1. Open [week1-code.R](week1-code.R) beside this page.
2. Work through the sections in order.
3. Run the matching block in RStudio.
4. Use the prompts here to practise explanation and model choice, not just syntax.
:::

## A. Explore the tourism dataset

This opening block introduces the tourism data and basic tsibble operations.

```r
library(fpp3)
tourism
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Loads the fpp3 package.
- Displays the tourism tsibble structure.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- The key variables: State, Region, Purpose.
- The time index is Quarter.
- The data spans 1998 Q1 to 2016 Q4.
:::

## B. Filter and summarise tourism data

This section shows how to filter for Victoria and summarise trips.

```r
tourism |>
  filter(State == "Victoria") |>
  summarise(Total_Trips = sum(Trips))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Filters the data to Victoria only.
- Sums the trips across all regions and purposes.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- The result is a single time series for Victoria's total trips.
- The index remains Quarter.
:::

## C. Explore PBS data

Shifting to the PBS dataset for pharmaceutical costs.

```r
PBS
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Displays the PBS tsibble.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Disaggregated by ATC2, Concession, Type.
- Time index is Month.
- Many series (84 × 2 × 2 = 336).
:::

## D. Filter PBS data

Filter for A10 drug type.

```r
PBS |> 
  filter(ATC2 == "A10")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Selects rows where ATC2 is "A10".
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Reduces to 4 series (2 Concession × 2 Type).
:::

## E. Select columns

Select specific columns from the filtered data.

```r
PBS |> 
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |> 
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Keeps only the specified columns.
- Index is always included.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Focuses on the cost variable.
:::

## F. Summarise over keys

Summarise total cost for A10.

```r
PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost) |>
  summarise(total_cost = sum(Cost))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Sums cost over the key variables.
- Results in a single time series.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Aggregation reduces multiple series to one.
:::

## G. Mutate to create new variables

Scale the cost to millions.

```r
PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost) |>
  summarise(total_cost = sum(Cost)) |>
  mutate(total_cost = total_cost / 1e6)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Divides total_cost by 1e6 to get millions.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Mutate adds or modifies columns.
- Useful for scaling or transformations.
:::

## H. Assign to variable

Create and assign the a10 object.

```r
a10 <- PBS |>
  filter(ATC2 == "A10") |>
  select(Month, Concession, Type, Cost) |>
  summarise(total_cost = sum(Cost)) |>
  mutate(total_cost = total_cost / 1e6)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this code is doing

- Pipes the operations and assigns to a10.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Assignment creates reusable objects.
- The pipe (%>%) chains operations.
:::
#| exercise: filter_summarise_tourism

library(qlcheckr)
apply_checks(
  c(
    "You need to load the fpp3 package!" = !("fpp3" %in% .packages()),

    "You need to use the summarise() function to sum over the Region and Purpose keys." = !search_ast(ql_ast(), .fn = summarise)
  )
)
```

## Hint

```r
tourism |>
  as_tibble() |>
  group_by(Region, Purpose)
```
:::

## Hint

After grouping, summarise the mean number of trips and filter for maximum trips.

```r
tourism |>
  as_tibble() |>
  group_by(Region, Purpose) |>
  summarise(Trips = mean(Trips), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(Trips == max(Trips))
```
